# PHS Population-Health Exemplar Move — composition proof

These four HTML artifacts are **rendered by the real expert-kernel board-grade
renderers** from an in-memory Presbyterian-Healthcare-Services-inspired
population-health Move — no database, no fabrication. They are the end-to-end
proof that the Pattern Pack Bible → Domain Function Pack encoding produces
excellent, grounded Move artifacts.

Regenerate with:

```
npx tsx scripts/phs/render-phs-population-health-exemplar.ts
```

## What they demonstrate

The Move binds the `(healthcare-provider, population_health_value_based_care)`
function pack — now carrying the own-it discipline (#3212) and the cross-cutting
architecture depth (#3213, via the Layer 7 solution-architecture outline). So:

- **`phs-solution-architecture.html`** — the architecture artifact inherits a
  real platform foundation: an inherited outline with a **"Platform landing zone
  & private data plane"** section and an **"Ingestion & data-integration
  framework (own-it)"** section that names DLT-META / the Databricks four-config
  framework / Lakeflow Connect and *rejects reinventing a bespoke framework or
  renting an outsourced destination platform*. The target architecture is built
  from the 5 curated domain reference patterns, each with a named boundary and
  human accountability point. This is the depth whose absence in the earlier PHS
  HTML started this whole work-stream.
- **`phs-discover-brief.html`** — reconciles the Move's 4 recorded baseline
  metrics against the pack's 12 operating metrics and **names the other 8 as
  honest seed gaps** ("Baseline coverage 33%"). No fabricated baselines.
- **`phs-business-case.html`** — the costed business case, calibrated by the
  pack's value model (cost-trend / RAF / quality components, each haircut).
- **`phs-mobilize-packet.html`** — the 30/60/90 mobilization packet.

All four are `bound: YES` — every claim is sourced from the curated function
pack, not improvised. An unbound Move would render an honest UNBOUND deck, never
a fabricated one.

## Known follow-on

The cross-cutting architecture foundation reaches the artifact through the
**Layer 7 deliverable outline** (which renders correctly), not through
`referenceSolutionPatterns` (Layer 4) — the architecture renderer treats Layer 4
as a mutually-exclusive option set and would render foundation layers as
"rejected alternatives". A foundation-aware renderer that presents
`cross-cutting-architecture-patterns.ts` as adopted foundation components is the
next enhancement.
